title: Prove an all-length balance law for native source-code controllers
body:
Ali Romman’s [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862) provides native identity transfers with an order-six source code, but a controller that restores the full source remains open. This adds a written, all-length conservation law for the fixed-code controller class: the signed count of forward/backward calls must be divisible by six, even with arbitrary invertible whole-bank scalar mixing, signs, scales, extra restored dirty banks and true inverse calls. Consequently every odd-call controller in that class is excluded, including a fixed-code substitution into the inherited nine-call skeleton. Coherently conjugated coordinate changes satisfy the same law.

A complementary theorem allows a different admissible chart at each call of an F-B-F exchange. Its unwanted diagonal block D satisfies `R D K = RK - 2I`; on the retained source this is `12 I_8`, so its rank is at least eight for every choice of those charts. This extends [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862)'s fixed-chart counterexample to all admissible selected rows in this architecture.

The contribution is one scoped proof package under `research/native-controller-congruence/`. It supplies a construction-level stopping criterion, rather than a bounded search or extra decimal digits. **The numerical multiplication bound is unchanged.** Port-dependent operations, non-equivariant physical chart transport, new clean workspace and paid repairs remain possible escape routes. The valid [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862) local construction is preserved; no native implementation or full supplier is claimed.

### Evidence

- The independent source extractor reads the selected [PR #1094](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094) archive, whose two local payloads exactly match [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862)'s pinned historical inputs. It checks the actual 112-port source matrix, the 96+16 code decomposition, the exact four-pair nine-stage recipe, and four changed-chart witnesses.
- Twelve separate dense-rational and CLI tests pass, including legal signs/scales, inverses, a six-call algebraic exchange positive control, noncentral matrix fixtures, missing hypotheses and corrupted inputs. No predecessor executable is imported.
- Registered Python 3.12.14 replay and optimized `-O` replay pass. The research-workflow suite passes (45 tests, three platform skips). Two agents independently reviewed proof scope and source extraction; this is not independent human review or proof-assistant verification.

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/native-controller-congruence
python3.12 -I -O -B research/native-controller-congruence/verify.py
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
```

`README.md` contains the proofs and precise reopening conditions; `TASK.json`, `SOURCES.json`, `ARCHIVE.json`, `PREDECESSOR.json`, `RESULT.json` and `VALIDATION.json` record scope, source pins and replay evidence. No full `make frontier1094-verify`, native routing, hosting, precision or all-size theorem replay is claimed.

### Provenance

Started from main `ecc75c79c22d909fd42aa68437eb77c4c1361835`, then rebased onto `ae95f60feec79897b153dba6459bb3f9fd4d7b8e`; consumed selected inputs are unchanged. The structural-track choice and change from the centre-path card are recorded. Final overlap search at 2026-10-14 15:33 UTC covered 538 open PRs and 599 discussion records with complete pagination; no remote match for the precise final terms was found, which is not a global novelty guarantee.

Credit Ali Romman's [PR #1862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1862) at `bb29ea73ad9be9a0c3d53cdcb1d22b2ee9ffe42f` for the code and native transfers, Chafik Boukhalfa's [PR #1877](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1877) at `6d455d2d71eb35ecf8e562711e5f719b994fe3f3` for the related original-logger obstruction, Jeremy Kothe’s [PR #1042](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1042), and Rohan Arun’s [PR #1094](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094), with the earlier gauge44/split-centres contributors retaining their attribution. Exact predecessor proof and notice are retained. Prepared for David Arias with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No selected frontier, frozen input, shared verifier or review ledger changes.
